details: JSON[create_time] undergoes required String checking at0x4902f8..0x490320; no null fallback. Parsing happens before subsequent server_id fields and before version dyn:toDouble at0x490620.
Devices stores the parsed DateTime in field_f, and toJson serializes that object rather than preserving original source spelling.
Malformed date throws at its original field position; version conversion must not be moved ahead of it.

claims.fraction_loop: 0x4913fc..0x491460, exactly6 digits, pad zeros, ignore further digits, never round
claims.timezone: 0x491488..0x491570; group8 present setsisUtc; numeric offset subtracts signed minutes before normalization
rules: ASCII optional signed4..6digit year; month/day2digits; separators and hour/minute/second according to original regex; suffix only inside optional time block.
Accept uppercase T or space, uppercase/lowercase Z, comma or decimal fractional second; no trimming or lowercase t; trailing line terminators are invalid.
Month/day/hour/minute/second accept overflow. Leap second60 normalizes into the next minute. Fraction limited to6microsecond digits.
Numeric offsets may have two-digit hours/minutes outside ordinary timezone ranges, and normalize arithmetically. Explicit suffix yields UTC; no suffix means local even when local zone is UTC.
Proleptic Gregorian calendar with astronomical year0; positive and negative months normalize using floor division.
0x491a18..0x491a6c execute64bit MUL/ADD without overflow checks, so some six-digit outlying years wrap into the permitted epoch range; Java long deliberately preserves that behavior.
Local parse has an extra preliminary one-day margin, then subtracts local offset; both UTC/local have finalabsolute range check.
millisecondsSinceEpoch floors negatives: -1microsecond -> -1millisecond; cached microsecond remains999.
_withValue calls_parts during microsecond validation at0x491710 and then_validate at0x49174c; format uses those cached parts.
extreme_exceptions: -290308-12-21T19:59:05.224192Z wraps exactly to signed64 minimum; abs and floor subtraction overflow and constructor validation raisesRangeError.

The same suffix-free input inAmerica/Los_Angeles reaches DateTime native offset guard withseconds=-18444944491255 and raisesArgumentError. This is reproduced without silently converting either into ordinary FormatException.

rules: Offset lookups whose floored seconds magnitude exceeds2147483647 map to a calendar-equivalent year in2008..2035 before the OS call. This is not unrestricted historical Java timezone lookup.
Dart local resolution uses sequential offsets and a two-hour earlier probe. Overlaps choose the earliest valid instant; gaps choose the earlier offset, moving the wall clock forward.
Native runtime/lib/date.cc rejects clampedseconds magnitude>2147483647; Java ArgumentError reproduces this guard.
Default parser uses TimeZone.getDefault(); explicitTimeZone overload is for deterministic offline testing. Parsed field parts are cached atconstruction.
limits: OS tzdata remains external. Same zone ID with different operating-system timezone database versions can give different offsets; six-zone sampled agreement is not all historical zone-rule equivalence.
The VM two-hour probe is retained, including its limitations for unusual multiple transitions; no replacement by Java atZone/lenientGregorianCalendar.

rules: ISO uses T, four-digit year within[-9999,9999], otherwise explicitsign and at least6digits.
toString uses a space and_fourDigits for every year, so year10000 is10000 rather than+010000.
Always3millisecond digits; append3microsecond digits onlywhenmicrosecond!=0. UTC endsZ; localhasnooffsetsuffix.
DateTime in Message.msg_content must use its own toString override, not ISO or Object_toString. This does not add supportforcustomreceiverclasses orcycles.
